claim: Traveling to conferences with children presents a number of logistical and financial challenges.
source: Traveling to conferences with children presents a number of logistical and financial challenges.
evidence: This is the main thesis statement of the manuscript, supported by detailed examples and discussion throughout the text.

claim: The environmental cost of air travel has been causing scientists to reconsider conference travel.
source: Recently, this discussion has broadened to include the environmental cost of air travel, which has also been causing scientists to reconsider conference travel (Langin, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Langin, 2019.

claim: Some institutions require conference attendance for promotion.
source: Gaining visibility is critical, with some institutions even requiring conference attendance for promotion, but conference travel may mean dipping into a limited start-up fund or spending time away from a fledgling laboratory.
evidence: Statement based on knowledge of institutional practices in academia.

claim: For single parents, lactating parents, parents of a child with a disability, parents who share caregiving with a working partner, or whose partner is attending the same conference, leaving children at home may be challenging or impossible.
source: For others, including single parents, lactating parents, parents of a child with a disability, parents who share caregiving with a working partner, or whose partner is attending the same conference, leaving children at home may be challenging or impossible.
evidence: Based on logical inference about the practical constraints faced by these specific groups of parents.

claim: Only certain academics, most often women, have to make the choice about bringing children to conferences.
source: It is important to remember that only certain academics, most often women, have to make this choice, so making either option as easy as possible is a critical step towards inclusivity – which in turn, leads to better science (Nielsen et al., 2017).
evidence: Based on knowledge of gender disparities in caregiving responsibilities in academia.

claim: Inclusivity leads to better science.
source: It is important to remember that only certain academics, most often women, have to make this choice, so making either option as easy as possible is a critical step towards inclusivity – which in turn, leads to better science (Nielsen et al., 2017).

source: This stacks the deck against academic parents, and disproportionately affects women, since biology, cultural and societal norms mean that they more often have to choose to bring their child with them or not travel at all.
evidence: Based on inference from the evidence presented about reimbursement challenges.
